meta.title: Jathag — Know your chart, not just your sign.
meta.description: Accurate Vedic birth charts, explained in short, honest, modern language. Free, no account, no ads. Beta, stars are being aligned.

betaNotice: Jathag Beta — The stars are still aligning. We are actively refining our features and design. Expect occasional shifts as we calibrate the cosmos.

hero.title: Know your chart, [not just your sign].
hero.intro: Jathag turns your birth details into an [accurate Vedic birth chart], then explains it in [short, honest, modern language]. No fear, no ads.

features.title: Accurate chart
features.text: Calculated from your exact birth date, time and place,
features.soonText: drawn in the style you know.

features.title: Plain-language explanations
features.text: Short, honest notes on what each part means. No jargon, no fear.

features.title: Your life timeline
features.text: Your dasha periods, the chapters of your life, laid out as a simple timeline.

form.title: Generate Your Chart
form.subtitle: Date, time and place of birth.

time.label: Time of birth
time.hint: The exact time, in hours and minutes, as written on the birth record.

place.label: Place of birth
place.hint: Type your town or city, e.g. Madurai. To narrow it down, add the state or country after a comma: Madurai, Tamil Nadu.
place.noResults: No places found. Try another spelling or a nearby town.
place.resultsCount: {count} places found. Use the up and down arrow keys to choose one.
place.resultsCountOne: 1 place found. Use the up and down arrow keys to choose it.

repeatedTime.question: This time happened twice that night: the clocks went back an hour. Which one was it?
repeatedTime.later: The second time (after the clocks went back)

form.privacy: Your details are only used to calculate your chart. Nothing is stored on our servers.

clockNote.buttonLabel: About the clock used for this date
clockNote.mumbai: In Mumbai until the 1950s, many people used Bombay time, 39 minutes behind IST. We've calculated your chart with IST. If your family used Bombay time, your chart may be different. You'll be able to switch soon.
clockNote.westBengal: In Kolkata and West Bengal until the late 1940s, many people used Calcutta time, 23 minutes 20 seconds ahead of IST. We've calculated your chart with IST. If your family used Calcutta time, your chart may be different. You'll be able to switch soon.
clockNote.warTime: From September 1942 to October 1945 India's official clock was War Time, one hour ahead of IST, and we've used it. If the time was written in IST, your chart may be different. You'll be able to switch soon.
clockNote.warTimeEarly: Between October 1941 and May 1942 some parts of India used War Time, one hour ahead of IST. We've calculated your chart with IST. If the time was written in War Time, your chart may be different. You'll be able to switch soon.
clockNote.before1906: Before 1906, many towns kept their own local time. Here that was about {minutes} minutes {direction} IST. We've calculated your chart with IST. If the time was written in local time, your chart may be different. You'll be able to switch soon.
clockNote.before1906OneMinute: Before 1906, many towns kept their own local time. Here that was about 1 minute {direction} IST. We've calculated your chart with IST. If the time was written in local time, your chart may be different. You'll be able to switch soon.
clockNote.before1906Same: Before 1906, many towns kept their own local time. Here it was within a minute of IST, so your chart is very unlikely to change. We've calculated your chart with IST.
clockNote.mumbaiWarTime: From September 1942 to October 1945 India's official clock was War Time, one hour ahead of IST, and we've used it. In Mumbai, many people also used Bombay time, 39 minutes behind IST. If the time was written in IST or in Bombay time, your chart may be different. You'll be able to switch soon.
clockNote.mumbaiWarTimeEarly: Between October 1941 and May 1942 some parts of India used War Time, one hour ahead of IST, and in Mumbai many people used Bombay time, 39 minutes behind IST. We've calculated your chart with IST. If the time was written in War Time or in Bombay time, your chart may be different. You'll be able to switch soon.
clockNote.westBengalWarTime: From September 1942 to October 1945 India's official clock was War Time, one hour ahead of IST, and we've used it. In Kolkata and West Bengal, many people also used Calcutta time, 23 minutes 20 seconds ahead of IST. If the time was written in IST or in Calcutta time, your chart may be different. You'll be able to switch soon.
clockNote.westBengalWarTimeEarly: Between October 1941 and May 1942 some parts of India used War Time, one hour ahead of IST, and in Kolkata and West Bengal many people used Calcutta time, 23 minutes 20 seconds ahead of IST. We've calculated your chart with IST. If the time was written in War Time or in Calcutta time, your chart may be different. You'll be able to switch soon.
clockNote.before1906NoPlace: Before 1906, many towns kept their own local time, up to about half an hour different from IST. We've calculated your chart with IST. If the time was written in local time, your chart may be different. You'll be able to switch soon.
